item.title: Scaling Local Solvers with the Many-Body Expansion
item.description: arXiv:2610.30137v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce a Many-Body Expansion framework for scaling black-box solvers for discrete optimization. The method decomposes a large problem into fragments, repeatedly improves each fragment with the rest of the assignment held fixed, and then applies targeted corrections on unions of fragments. The solver itself is unchanged: it only receives a restricted subproblem and returns a candidate assignment. The framework separates decomposition from solver design. Moebius inversion gives an exact fragment expansion of the objective, and for pairwise objectives such as graph coloring, MAX-CUT, and QUBO the expansion closes at second order. The promoted solver is monotone by construction, terminates in finitely many productive sweeps for non-negative integer-valued objectives, and connects to junction-tree dynamic programming when the fragment interaction structure is acyclic and full response functions are propagated. On graph coloring benchmarks, the promoted versions of TabuSearch and simulated annealing (SA) generally outperform flat applications of the same solvers, often finding better solutions in less CPU time, and the gain proves insensitive to the choice of graph partition. A facility-location study delimits the claim: there the partition must respect the objective's interaction locality, and the promoted solver reaches within 0.3-1.4% of GLPK-certified optima at every tested size. The same wrapper interface is used in each solver-swap case, and the facility-location check reuses the same monotone guard with a sign-adjusted interaction diagnostic; the improvements therefore come from the MBE promotion mechanism rather than solver-specific tuning.
item.dc:creator: Federico Zahariev (Iowa State University, Ames Laboratory), Amr Sabry (Indiana University)

item.title: A General Variable Neighborhood Search for Logistic Network Flow Design with Nonlinear Edge Costs and Transshipment Capacities
item.description: arXiv:2610.30139v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the problem of routing multiple commodities through a logistic transport network so as to minimise the joint cost of vehicle movements and of transshipment (reload) operations at intermediate storages. The problem combines two features that are common in practice but rarely treated together: edge costs that are nonlinear in the transported volume, because freight is carried by vehicles of fixed capacity, and hard upper bounds on the volume that can be reloaded at each node. We formulate the problem as a mixed integer linear program in both an arc-based and a path-based form, derive its linear relaxation, and propose a metaheuristic solver based on General Variable Neighborhood Search (GVNS). The method works in the path space and relies on three problem-specific neighborhoods that generate new candidate paths by (i) shortest paths under a reload-aware metric, (ii) edges carrying partially loaded vehicles, and (iii) detours around congested storages. We evaluate the method on our open benchmark for this problem (arXiv:2606.20653): a corpus of realistic logistic networks calibrated on real road graphs of nine European countries, five U.S. states and the European part of Russia, with near-planar topology (Zipf city sizes, a spatial-network budget model, and a doubly constrained gravity demand model). On 35 synthetic and 15 real-geometry instances with up to 150 storages, GVNS returns solutions within about one percent of the best dual bound on small networks -- a branch-and-bound lower bound substantially tighter than the LP relaxation -- is stable across random seeds, and for a comparable wall-clock budget is up to 55% better than a time-limited exact solver on the medium instances.
item.dc:creator: Varvara Kovaleva, Alexander Ponomarenko

item.title: The SMFCE Paradigm: A Unified Modeling Framework Based on State, Cost, and Extremal Evolution
item.description: arXiv:2610.30140v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper proposes a unified modeling framework centered on "state-cost-extremal evolution," referred to as the SMFCE paradigm. The paradigm represents the effective state of a system as a point in a state space, characterizes state cost by a single-valued scalar field, and describes system evolution through local cost descent or local extremum selection. Its mathematical core employs classical tools from differential geometry, gradient systems, and dynamical systems. The contribution of this paper is not to reintroduce these foundational results, but to organize them into two operational modeling principles. On finite-dimensional smooth Riemannian manifolds under appropriate regularity conditions, the path independence of cost differences and the cost monotonicity of negative gradient flows follow directly from classical results, while the descent property of discrete local-minimum transitions follows directly from the definition of a minimum. For same-level iterative emergence and present-centeredness, the paper provides conditional mathematical formulations using, respectively, parameterized gradient systems and bifurcation theory, and Markov processes and receding-horizon optimization. The paper further introduces three layered metrics: cost quantity, directed coupling degree, and commitment fulfillment rate, at the state, transition, path, and system levels. Finally, the paper discusses semantic modeling of large language model training and inference within this framework, explicitly distinguishes classical mathematical results, conditional propositions, and empirical adaptation models, and provides reproducible empirical testing procedures for the two modeling principles.
item.dc:creator: Wei Ba, Ang Fu, Shengsong Kong, Zhongchuan Fu

item.title: Consensus-Aware Co-design of Wireless Multi-Agent Control and Communication Systems
item.description: arXiv:2610.30141v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Autonomous multi-agent control systems (MACSs) enable distributed coordination in emerging applications such as smart power grids and autonomous vehicle or drone networks. In many of these applications, inter-agent communication relies on wireless networks. However, conventional MACS designs neglect the interaction between the communication and control subsystems. At the same time, conventional wireless designs reserve communication resources based on worst-case MACS requirements. Consequently, control performance is degraded and wireless resources are utilized inefficiently. To address these challenges, we propose a consensus-aware co-design approach for MACSs and wireless communication systems. We introduce a system model in which agents achieve consensus by exchanging information through device-to-device (D2D) links that share spectrum with cellular users under limited bandwidth resources. Based on this model, we formulate a joint optimization problem for consensus-topology selection and wireless resource allocation to minimize bandwidth consumption while guaranteeing consensus and satisfying the quality-of-service (QoS) requirements of both MACSs and cellular users. Although the resulting problem is a mixed-integer nonlinear program (NP-hard in general), a structural property of the optimal solution enables a sequential two-stage optimization algorithm with polynomial complexity. Simulations on a smart power grid case study demonstrate that the proposed approach achieves 24-27% bandwidth savings compared with the two baselines while maintaining consensus and satisfying all QoS requirements of the control agents and the communication users.
item.dc:creator: Atefeh Termehchi, Sajedeh Soleimani, Shiva Kazemi Taskooh, Mehdi Rasti, Ekram Hossain

item.title: Strongly Regular Graph Construction via Quadratic Binary Optimization
item.description: arXiv:2610.30142v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Strongly regular graphs, hereafter SRGs, are highly structured combinatorial objects of central interest in algebraic graph theory and quantum information, whose explicit construction becomes rapidly intractable as the number of vertices grows; Conway's still unresolved $99$-graph problem is an emblematic example. The matrix equation defining SRGs is quadratic in the binary edge variables, so the natural penalty enforcing it, a sum of squared residuals, is quartic and lies outside quadratic unconstrained binary optimization, known as QUBO. We prove a considerably stronger obstruction, namely that no quadratic function of the edge variables has the labeled SRGs as its exact set of global minimizers, except for three degenerate families given by the perfect matchings, the cocktail-party graphs and the pentagon. In particular, we formally establish that the $99$-vertex graph of Conway's problem cannot be obtained from any QUBO over the edge variables without auxiliary variables. Guided by this theorem we develop two complementary algorithms. The first operates within pure QUBO, solves the degenerate families exactly, and beyond them works as a generate--prune--verify pipeline whose output is a reduced set of candidates certified by a polynomial-time classical test. The second solves the full problem by quadratizing this quartic penalty through Rosenberg auxiliary variables, whose number grows as $\Theta(N^3)$ with the number of vertices $N$. We test the pure-QUBO route under simulated annealing on all feasible families with at most $18$ vertices and the auxiliary-variable route on representative targets up to $16$ vertices, and tabulate the algebraically feasible parameter sets for graphs with at most $49$ vertices.
item.dc:creator: D. Osorio, P. Andagana, V. Gonz\'alez, J. Czartowski, D. Goyeneche

item.title: The Last Iterate of the Projected Stochastic Subgradient Method Pays a Logarithm, Even in Dimension One
item.description: arXiv:2610.30143v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that the projected stochastic subgradient method with the standard anytime stepsizes $\eta_t = \gamma/\sqrt t$ can suffer expected last-iterate optimization error of order $(\log n)/\sqrt n$ already on the real line. Combined with the classical in-expectation upper bound, this establishes the sharp worst-case order of the projected stochastic subgradient method.
item.dc:creator: Guglielmo Beretta, Tommaso Cesari, Roberto Colomboni

item.title: Forward Tangent-Centered Sinkhorn DRO: Exact Nominal Recovery from Optimal Transport to KL
item.description: arXiv:2610.30144v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Fixed-reference entropy-regularized transport yields smooth distributionally robust optimization (DRO) objectives, but its value as a function of the adversarial marginal is generally minimized at a kernel-smoothed law rather than at the nominal distribution. Consequently, the smallest raw ambiguity set need not recover nominal risk. Building on prior information-geometric plan-KL orientations, we study the forward tangent-centered discrepancy obtained by subtracting the value and first variation at the nominal law. This is the unique affine recentering, up to the simplex gauge; for symmetric costs, its plan-KL representation coincides with the forward candidate noted by Amari et al. (2018). The representation shows that the discrepancy dominates marginal KL, is uniquely zero at the nominal law, and is strongly convex in total variation. The resulting DRO problem retains a scalar log-sum-exp dual and closed-form conditional adversarial weights. On finite supports with symmetric zero-diagonal costs, the discrepancy converges uniformly to the unregularized transport cost at low temperature; for any finite cost, its rescaled value converges uniformly to marginal KL at high temperature. We derive its exact local Hessian, an explicit finite-sample containment radius, and a generalized chi-square calibration for multinomial data. Controlled simulations verify nominal centering, both limiting regimes, and practical plug-in coverage.
item.dc:creator: Junjie Guo

item.title: Elimination Geometry II: Integrability, Representation, and Structural Limits
item.description: arXiv:2610.30145v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Elimination geometry studies the exact nonnegative defect left after an auxiliary variable is optimized out. Part~II audits this certified-elimination interface through three theorem families. For integrability, local gaps form a repeated partial-elimination tower precisely under nonnegativity, touching, and zero elementary-square circulation. Hodge projection constructs nearest finite-space repairs and separates curvature, certification, and global period taxes. For representation and price, a descent gate characterizes surjective refinements and rules out strictly convex separable, duplication-invariant weight penalties. Dummy and target-calling lifts show that unrestricted lift design is vacuous, whereas the Fidelity-coherence frontier isolates irreducible cost. A modal Gram block classifies unconstrained quadratic lift-coupling germs and yields aligned Gaussian risk ledgers. Bernstein spectral functions preserve graph-Laplacian structure. Graph-universal Markov resolvents exist exactly up to first-order fractional qualification, and universal polynomial spectral penalties reduce to nonnegative Laplacian multiples. This linear limit does not preclude Part~I's nonlinear CDF repair and sharp CRPS theory. For converses, finite-order target-jet preservation uniquely requires subtraction of the corresponding defect jet, up to flat terms; approximate jets yield quasi-descent and stationary limits. Fixed-marginal coupling obeys a dependence-benefit frontier. Reversing certified KL in entropy-regularized control eliminates dimension-free guarantees, while a fixed measurement preserves all Umegaki defects of a faithful Gibbs family exactly when that family commutes.
item.dc:creator: Mian Huang, Xueqin Wang

item.title: A reciprocal graph-deviation functional: structural identifiability from controlled equilibrium maps
item.description: arXiv:2610.30146v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We constructed a reciprocal graph-deviation functional for positive ratios on a finite weighted graph. Its scalar generator $J(x)=\tfrac12(x+x^{-1})-1$ was characterized previously by ratio-composition and unit log-curvature. Our principal new result was structural identifiability: already on a two-site, one-edge system, the complete minimizer-location map obtained by sweeping the boundary and site-to-edge weight ratio determines any reciprocal generator whose log-coordinate representation is $C^2$ with everywhere-positive curvature, up to a positive scale; unit-curvature calibration fixes that scale. For the calibrated reciprocal family~$J_p$ we obtained the equilibrium response in closed form. A synthetic $15$-condition sweep with seven simulated measurements per condition and log-scale noise $\sigma=0.05$ selected $J$ over~$J_{1.1}$ with probability~$0.997$ under exact boundary and weight parameters; a declared representation-uncertainty screen lowered that value to approximately~$0.88$. These probabilities characterize the simulated design under the declared data-generating model. The finite sweep discriminated prespecified generators, whereas nonparametric recovery required the complete response map. We also recorded the associated convex gradient-flow and Langevin dynamics.
item.dc:creator: Jonathan Washburn, Megan Simons

item.title: Sufficient Conditions for Exact Convergence Time in Prescribed-Time Control
item.description: arXiv:2610.30147v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we propose a series of theoretical results for prescribed-time control to rigorously prove that the closed-loop system will not reach the equilibrium point before the prescribed time. Thus, it is convenient to prove that the settling time is exactly equal to the prescribed time instant. In other words, conservative estimation of the settling time, which often accompanies classical finite-/fixed-time or prescribed-time control results, is theoretically avoided in this paper. Specifically, we introduce a local Lipschitz condition, a local homogeneous linear-growth condition, and an Osgood condition in sequence. Both reduction to absurdity and the Lyapunov method are applied to demonstrate that the system cannot converge to zero before the prescribed time instant. Finally, the proposed framework is applied to prescribed-time controllers based on adaptive backstepping, parametric Lyapunov equations, and distributed leader-following consensus, demonstrating the generality of the proposed results.
item.dc:creator: Jiyuan Kuang

item.title: Do Machine Learning-Guided Proactive Full Capacity Protocols Mitigate Emergency Department Overcrowding? A Simulation-Based Evaluation
item.description: arXiv:2610.30148v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Objective: Emergency department (ED) overcrowding threatens care quality, yet Full Capacity Protocols (FCPs) are typically activated only after crowding thresholds have been exceeded. This study evaluated whether machine learning-guided proactive FCP activation improves ED crowding control compared with conventional reactive activation. Materials and Methods: We developed and validated an integrated machine learning and discrete-event simulation framework representing ED patient flow and capacity management. An embedded machine learning model predicted hourly waiting-room crowding six hours ahead and triggered proactive FCP activation. Using empirically calibrated operational parameters from a large US hospital, we compared proactive and reactive deployment strategies over a 365-day simulation horizon with 10 independent replications. Outcomes included ED length of stay, wait time, percentage of time above the crowding threshold, number of FCP activations, and protocol duration. Results: Proactive deployment produced statistically significant reductions in the percentage of time above the crowding threshold and average protocol duration across all threshold settings. It also reduced crowding variability and extreme congestion events, resulting in smoother ED operations. Although proactive deployment generally improved ED length of stay and wait time, these differences were not statistically significant. Conclusion: Embedding machine learning predictions within an operational simulation enables proactive, prediction-guided capacity management before severe congestion develops. These findings support the feasibility and potential value of proactive FCP deployment as a decision-support strategy for improving ED crowding control and provide evidence to support prospective implementation in clinical practice.
item.dc:creator: Khalid Aram, Orhun Vural, Bunyamin Ozaydin, James Booth, Abdulaziz Ahmed

item.title: A Tutte-Like Theorem for Injective Flows on Meshes
item.description: arXiv:2610.30149v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This work proves a theorem regarding injectivity of continuous flows that are defined via discrete vector fields on triangle meshes. In similar fashion to Tutte's embedding, the theorem shows a connection between harmonicity and injectivity. Specifically, a discrete harmonic function is computed over a spherical mesh, and its $90^\circ$-rotated gradients are taken as the vector field. We show that this leads to an injective flow over the mesh, i.e., when two points are advected along the vector field, their trajectories are guaranteed to not intersect. The core insight behind this theorem is that the characterization of the Poincar\'e-Hopf indices of discrete harmonic 1-forms is paralleled in the combinatorial rules for injective vector fields. Similarly to Tutte's embedding, the injective vector field can be computed by simply solving a sparse linear system. Furthermore, it is differentiably dependent on the entries of the Laplacian, enabling unconstrained gradient-based optimization of the vector field while preserving injectivity. The advection itself can be computed by a quick and accurate algorithm. We experimentally validate the injectivity of the results, as well as show examples of differentiable optimization, such as computing an injective approximation to a given non-injective vector field, and fitting an injective vector field to satisfy constraints.
item.dc:creator: Darsh Kaushik, Noam Aigerman

item.title: The Gittins Index for a Transparent One-Armed Bandit with a Continuous Payoff Spectrum in Equilibrium States
item.description: arXiv:2610.30150v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present an analogue of the classical Gittins index for a one-armed decision problem with a continuous spectrum of payoffs. The model assumes that the decision-maker observes independent realizations of a random variable and, at each step, decides whether to accept the current opportunity or continue observing. We show that the optimal strategy takes the form of a threshold rule, while the corresponding reservation index is determined by a one-dimensional fixed-point equation with a direct decision-theoretic interpretation. The model is illustrated with an example of bookmaker betting related to horse racing and the Kelly criterion. This perspective allows the proposed index to be viewed as a threshold of informational advantage. This, in turn, points to potential applications in optimal stopping problems and decision-making under uncertainty.
item.dc:creator: Marcin Makowski, Edward W. Piotrowski, Jan L. Cie\'sli\'nski

item.title: Advance versus Spot Selling in Queueing Systems: the Effect of Uncertainty Sources
item.description: arXiv:2610.30156v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop an unobservable M/M/1 queueing model to analyze advance selling and spot selling under uncertainty. Customers are heterogeneous in waiting costs, drawn from a uniform distribution. We disentangle two fundamental sources of uncertainty: customer valuation and service capacity. We derive the respective revenue functions for both advance and spot selling strategies and compare their performance. Our analysis reveals that advance selling is more profitable when customer valuations are uncertain. Conversely, spot selling emerges as the more profitable strategy when uncertainty originates from service capacity. When both sources are present, our numerical experiments suggest that the preferred regime depends on the relative dispersion of the two uncertainties: advance selling tends to be favored when valuation uncertainty is sufficiently pronounced relative to capacity uncertainty, whereas spot selling tends to be favored when capacity uncertainty is more pronounced. These results highlight how the origin and magnitude of uncertainty shape the optimal selling strategy in service queues and offer practical guidance for platforms and service providers deciding between advance and spot selling.
item.dc:creator: Yumeng Liu, Dongyuan Zhan

item.title: Ergodic Linear-Quadratic Optimal Control with Stochastic Coefficients
item.description: arXiv:2610.30219v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate ergodic linear-quadratic optimal control problems with stochastic coefficients and introduce the associated stochastic ergodic Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman (HJB) equation, in which the classical ergodic constant is replaced by a random process $\lambda$. We establish well-posedness of the equation and show that $\lambda$ characterizes the optimal ergodic costs for a general class of averaging kernels, including those corresponding to normalized finite-horizon and discounted costs. For random-periodic coefficients, we construct a random-periodic solution and show that the optimal ergodic costs associated with all admissible averaging kernels coincide. We also establish stability of the optimal ergodic costs under perturbations of the coefficients.
item.dc:creator: Xuyang Lin, Nizar Touzi

item.title: Continuous-time analysis and algorithms for linear and convex quadratic programs via exactly solvable differential inclusions
item.description: arXiv:2610.30300v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Linear and convex quadratic programs are fundamental problems in optimization. While many methods have been developed for solving these programs in large-scale applications, to our knowledge none have attempted to solve their continuous-time gradient flow, a differential inclusion, in full generality without assumptions beyond feasibility. Recent work solved the gradient flows in two special cases, basis pursuit and the lasso, and obtained competitive algorithms. Motivated by these results, we solve the general case exactly. Using the minimal selection principle for monotone differential inclusions, we show that the trajectory of the gradient flow consists of finitely many pieces, each obtained from one nonnegative least-squares problem. Its final piece yields an optimal solution or a certificate of unboundedness. This analysis leads to two algorithms. The first algorithm is exact, terminates after finitely many steps, and applies to linear programs and projections onto polyhedra. The second algorithm, which we call minimal selection descent, discretizes the gradient flow for general convex quadratic programs. Its iterates converge to an optimal solution when one exists and otherwise certify unboundedness. We apply both algorithms to a positivity-preserving limiter for a discontinuous Galerkin scheme and to optimal control problems for the Poisson and heat equations. In the limiter, the first algorithm conserves the total mass more accurately than the state-of-the-art Douglas--Rachford splitting method. On the control problems, minimal selection descent reaches the optimal value to machine precision and is competitive in time with commercial and open-source solvers.
item.dc:creator: Gabriel P. Langlois, Akwum Onwunta, J\'er\^ome Darbon

item.title: A Transformer-based Approach for Real-time Multi-agent Path Planning with Varying Initial/Final Conditions
item.description: arXiv:2610.30388v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We address the problem of real-time multi-agent path planning under prescribed initial and final configurations, formulated as a high-dimensional optimal control problem subject to inter-agent collision avoidance and obstacle constraints. Classical solvers based on the Hamilton--Jacobi--Bellman equation or Pontryagin's maximum principle (PMP) become computationally intractable as the number of agents grows, due to the curse of dimensionality and the non-convexity introduced by interaction constraints. We propose OCFormer, a transformer-based neural network that parameterizes the inverse of a coordinate transformation mapping a simple, analytically tractable latent space, in which agents evolve independently under a decoupled Hamiltonian, to the physical space of the coupled, interacting system. The model is trained by minimizing a physics-informed loss comprising the Hamiltonian ODE residual from the PMP and a boundary matching term, without requiring pre-computed trajectory data. The self-attention mechanism endows OCFormer with permutation equivariance over agents, a structural symmetry that prior symplectic network approaches do not natively enforce. When trained on a distribution of boundary conditions, the amortized OCFormer produces near-optimal trajectories for unseen initial and final configurations in a single forward pass ($\sim$220ms), enabling real-time inference without retraining. We further introduce a lightweight transfer learning framework that adapts a pretrained OCFormer to out-of-distribution perturbations in seconds via L-BFGS fine-tuning. Numerical experiments on two- and three-dimensional multi-agent navigation with up to 128 agents demonstrate the scalability and efficiency of the proposed approach.
item.dc:creator: Qian Zhang, Shanqing Liu, Jerome Darbon, George Karniadakis

item.title: Soft-Update MSA for Nonconvex Stochastic Optimal Control: Theory and Algorithms
item.description: arXiv:2610.30585v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For the method of successive approximations (MSA), a fundamental challenge is that the stochastic maximum principle (SMP) provides an optimality condition rather than a descent rule. To overcome this difficulty for nonconvex stochastic control problems, we develop a soft-update MSA (SU-MSA) with a second-order-adjoint correction of the Hamiltonian and a neural realization called DeepSMP. Both an explicit stepsize rule guaranteeing cost descent and the convergence of the algorithm are established. Moreover, the global SMP condition is asymptotically satisfied when the corrected Hamiltonian is convex, while in a special case the cost is further proved to converge to the global optimum. To extend SU-MSA to high dimensions, we develop DeepSMP using a differentiable smooth approximation of the corrected Hamiltonian and analyze the convergence of the resulting objective and its gradient. Numerical experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework.
item.dc:creator: Shaolin Ji, Xinmeng Liu

item.title: Retraction-Free Nonsmooth Optimization on the Stiefel Manifold: Subgradient and Proximal Landing Methods
item.description: arXiv:2610.30617v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop three retraction-free Landing methods for nonsmooth composite optimization over the Stiefel manifold, combining an (approximately) tangential direction with an infeasibility-reducing normal direction. The subgradient Landing method, with normal stepsizes parameterized by $\alpha\in[0,1]$, has best-iterate complexity bounds $\mathcal{O}(\epsilon^{-4})$ for surrogate stationarity and $\mathcal{O}(\epsilon^{-2/(2-\alpha)})$ for feasibility. For $\alpha=0$, it converges locally $R$-linearly under local weak sharpness and mild assumptions. The proximal gradient Landing method computes a tangential direction by solving a proximal subproblem and combines it with the same normal direction. Moreover, the inexact proximal gradient Landing method allows the proximal subproblem to be solved approximately and applies an explicit correction to control violations of the tangency condition. Both proximal methods have outer-iteration complexity bounds $\mathcal{O}(\epsilon^{-2})$ for stationarity and $\mathcal{O}(\epsilon^{-1})$ for feasibility, and every accumulation point is first-order stationary. Under an additional asymptotic Bregman-error condition and the Kurdyka-Lojasiewicz property of a suitable auxiliary function, the primal sequence of the inexact method converges to a first-order stationary point. Numerical experiments illustrate the effectiveness of all three methods. On the tested sparse principal component analysis instances, the inexact method has favorable running times, and both proximal methods maintain small feasibility residuals.
item.dc:creator: Zilong Cui, Tongxin Hu, Bin Gao, Ran Gu

item.title: Adaptive Restart under Unknown KL Geometry in Stochastic Weakly-Convex Optimization
item.description: arXiv:2610.30650v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: KL geometry accelerates restart schedules in stochastic weakly-convex optimization, but the schedule depends jointly on an unknown and potentially nonunique geometric description. We introduce CARP-KL, a certified portfolio that adapts over valid KL descriptions while using the same primitive stochastic-subgradient oracle for both optimization and candidate selection. Over declared polynomial parameter ranges, CARP-KL competes with every affordable valid description and preserves the known-description polynomial Moreau-stationarity rate up to logarithmic factors, without objective values, an exact proximal map, direct Moreau-gradient access, or a bounded-domain assumption. Controlled experiments quantify the finite-budget price of this universality. The portfolio repeatedly contains strong candidates, while certification consumes a substantial share of the oracle budget and finite-sample ranking limits their recovery. A common conservative gap bound further reduces the portfolio from $O(\log^3 T)$ to $O(\log^2 T)$ candidates with an explicit scale-mismatch penalty. The theory and diagnostics together establish certified unknown-geometry adaptation and pinpoint selection as the principal practical frontier of the current construction.
item.dc:creator: Binh T. Nguyen, Khoa D. Nguyen, Bao Thai Huynh

item.title: Hidden Convexity of the Joint Range of Three Quadratic Forms and Applications
item.description: arXiv:2610.30706v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate a hidden convexity phenomenon for triples of homogeneous quadratic forms. We give a complete characterization of the convexity of the upper image obtained by adding the nonnegative orthant to their joint range. More precisely, the upper image is convex if and only if either a nonzero nonnegative linear combination of the three associated matrices is positive semidefinite, or the three quadratic forms admit a common strict negative direction. In particular, the upper image is convex whenever one of the three quadratic forms is convex. As applications, we establish the convexity of an associated value function and derive a generalized S-lemma for implications involving two quadratic inequalities and a strict theorem of the alternative for quadratic systems.
item.dc:creator: Tuan Ngoc Hoang, Huy Quang Nguyen

item.title: Assortment optimization under the perception-adjusted Luce model
item.description: arXiv:2610.30904v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Perception-Adjusted Luce Model (PALM) introduced by by Echenique et al. (2018) is a sequential choice model that can accommodate violations of regularity and choice overload, behaviors not captured by the utility-maximization framework. Flores et al. (2019) studied the assortment problem under the PALM and proved that, for the case of two levels, there is always an optimal solution that is revenue-ordered by level. They also conjectured that revenue-ordered by levels remain optimal for the general PALM with any number of levels. We resolve this question in the affirmative by showing that every PALM instance admits an optimal assortment that includes, within each level, all products at or above a level-specific revenue threshold. The proof involves first showing how the conjecture which deals with a discrete optimization problem, can be reduced to proving certain property of a related continuous optimization problem. Specifically, we study a continuous refinement of the assortment decision under the same PALM choice rule. Although the refinement permits partial utility selections, we prove it always has an optimum that selects complete revenue tiers. This allows us to show that the assortment problem is polynomial-time solvable when the number of levels is fixed.
item.dc:creator: Gerardo Berbeglia, Mashbat Suzuki, Matthew Tam

item.title: Safety-constrained position tracking of a flexible transmission system
item.description: arXiv:2610.31061v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider safety-constrained position tracking for a flexible transmission system consisting of a torsional shaft driven by a motor and connected to a gravitationally loaded inertia. The coupled PDE-ODE dynamics admit a semilinear formulation in which the linear input-output system is impedance passive and the gravitational torque enters as a bounded, globally Lipschitz perturbation. We establish an energy dissipation inequality for the nonlinear model and show that a position-funnel controller with supervised damping admits a unique global closed-loop trajectory. In particular, the motor-angle tracking error remains strictly inside a prescribed time-varying funnel, which can be chosen to enforce safety bounds on the motor angle.
item.dc:creator: Anthony Hastir, Timo Reis

item.title: Policy Evaluation and Policy Gradient for Continuous-Time Markov Regime-Switching Systems
item.description: arXiv:2610.31094v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study policy evaluation (PE) and policy gradient (PG) for continuous-time stochastic control with Markov regime-switching. The main challenges are the coexistence of diffusion and regime jumps, the coupling of regime-dependent value functions, and the construction of model-free learning rules from the coupled generators. We establish a martingale characterization of PE that incorporates both Brownian and switching martingales, and extend martingale loss and orthogonality methods to this setting. We further derive a coupled PG equation and a trajectory-based gradient representation that, under an action-independent switching generator, avoids explicit knowledge of the system coefficients and transition rates. These results lead to offline and online actor-critic algorithms. We also establish convergence and study the finite-grid approximation required for implementation. Numerical experiments for a regime-switching linear-quadratic problem illustrate the proposed methods.
item.dc:creator: Minghui Zhang, Xun Li, Xin Zhang

item.title: On Modified Newton Methods for Unconstrained Optimization Based on Lanczos Tridiagonalization
item.description: arXiv:2610.31110v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a strongly convex unconstrained minimization problem, Newton's method with a line search offers rapid convergence to a minimizer by incorporating second-order information. However, for a general unconstrained problem the Hessian need not be positive definite, which can lead to the inability to find a search direction or to search directions that fail to produce descent. Modified Newton methods are designed to handle this situation. This paper considers modifications to a Newton-conjugate-gradient approach based on Lanczos tridiagonalization. Existing methods are extended using dynamic modification schemes that provide a descent direction while keeping the modification bounded. A Lanczos-based scheme and a conjugate-gradient (CG)-based scheme are formulated and analyzed. These methods are mathematically equivalent in exact arithmetic, but their practical behavior differs in finite precision. Finally, it is shown how the convergence and computational cost are affected by varying the amount of additional curvature introduced and by allowing the early termination of the inner iterations.
item.dc:creator: Aban Ansari-\"Onnestam, Anders Forsgren, Philip E. Gill

item.title: Exact value functions and sensitivities for energy storage by fast Legendre transforms
item.description: arXiv:2610.31213v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Long chains of decisions coupled only through a bounded cumulative state, such as the operation of an energy-storage device, form convex programs that generic solvers treat as arbitrary sparse models. We present an exact solver for this class that propagates the complete convex cost-to-reach function through restrictions and infimal convolutions, each evaluated by fast Legendre-Fenchel conjugation as an ordered merge of slopes: no state grid, no value approximation, and a function rather than a single primal-dual pair as output. Price-taking storage instances of 5,000 to 15,000 hourly steps solve 35-93 times faster than Gurobi. The value function is what pays: exact capacity marginals in one differentiated pass, recourse assembled rather than sampled on scenario trees, and a certified sizing loop whose cut count does not grow with the number of weather years. We then widen the carried state. Two storages at one node can be eliminated rather than coordinated by carrying the value function of the pair, and we prove that this object is combinatorially rigid: every breakline the recursion realizes is vertical, horizontal, or borne by a line through the origin, with no genericity assumption. For d co-located stores sharing one charge-discharge coefficient, every realized wall is a position hyperplane or an indifference hyperplane {s_i = s_j}. A catalogue law maps where speed holds: one-dimensional chains beat the frontal solve by 15-30x and growing, while the planar block loses by 13.5-107x on rich network curves. Those curves are themselves exact, traced by a parametric dual simplex. The open-source package FLToptim, every benchmark driver and all data accompany the paper.
item.dc:creator: Robin Girard

item.title: Exact controllability and rapid stabilization of linear difference delay equations and one-dimensional hyperbolic systems
item.description: arXiv:2610.31225v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper addresses exact controllability and rapid stabilization issues for linear difference delay systems with finitely many pointwise delays. We first establish a criterion for exact controllability in $L^r$, $r \in [1, +\infty)$, characterized by a necessary and sufficient Hautus-type frequency-domain condition. The sufficiency of this condition in $L^r$ was already known [https://hal.science/hal-04830757/], whereas its necessity had previously been established only in $L^1$ [arXiv:2210.13590]. We answer [arXiv:2210.13590, Conjecture 3.8] by proving that this condition is also necessary for $r \in (1, +\infty)$. The analysis is based on rewriting the system as an evolution equation in a suitable Banach space, which allows one to apply duality arguments in the spirit of [https://doi.org/10.1137/S036301299119795X]. Building on this controllability analysis and the abstract stabilization framework developed in [https://doi.org/10.1137/S0363012996301609, arXiv:1301.5744], we prove that our exact controllability criterion in $L^r$ is also a sufficient condition for rapid stabilization in $L^2$, i.e., that the system of interest can be stabilized by a family of state feedback control laws ensuring that the closed-loop system is exponentially stable in $L^2$ with an arbitrarily large decay rate. As an application, we extend our results to linear one-dimensional hyperbolic partial differential equations, which can be reduced to linear difference delay systems via the method of characteristics, obtaining also a necessary and sufficient frequency-domain criterion for exact controllability in $L^r$, $r\in [1, +\infty)$, which, as before, is a sufficient condition for rapid stabilization in $L^2$.
item.dc:creator: Yacine Chitour, S\'ebastien Fueyo, Pierre Lissy, Guilherme Mazanti

item.title: Strong Duality Thresholds and Minimum Curvature for the Nearest Rectangular Symplectic Matrix Problem
item.description: arXiv:2610.31298v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the nearest rectangular symplectic matrix problem in the squared Frobenius norm for arbitrary targets $T\in\mathbb R^{2n\times2k}$, with $n\ge k$. We prove that its semidefinite relaxation is exact for every target if and only if $n\ge2k-1$. Under this condition, the primal problem, the relaxation, and both Lagrangian dual problems attain the same optimal value. In this range, we derive the exact minimum Rayleigh quotient of the Riemannian Hessian at every feasible point under the Euclidean induced metric, and prove that all second-order stationary points are global minimizers. We also obtain global objective error bounds. We extend the strong-duality and minimum-curvature results to Hermitian positive definite row weights, proving that strong duality holds for every target if and only if the lowest eigenvalue of the weight has complex multiplicity at least $2k-1$. The dual formulation leads to a method whose main iterations use matrices of order $2k$, with $O(k^2)$ iterative storage apart from the full input and output. Across six tested sizes, mean-time speedups are $2.55$--$12.60$ over a Riemannian first-order method and $4.61$--$43.93$ over Jensen--Zimmermann R--TR2; batching gives a further factor of $3.45$--$23.53$ over sequential calls. The theoretical results complete the critical dimensions not covered by Gram convexification and quadratic matrix programming.
item.dc:creator: Yulin Xie, Aiqing Zhu, Yifa Tang

item.title: Gradient Discrete Schrodinger Bridge Matching for Peptide Generation
item.description: arXiv:2610.31361v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The optimal control of a discrete Schr\"odinger bridge is a discrete gradient, a difference of vertex potentials, but recent models such as MadSBM instead learn a free control on the edges by cross-entropy. We prove that this leaves the action uncontrolled: cross-entropy identifies the control only up to a state-dependent shift (a gauge), and the action is $\operatorname{KL}(r\|p)$ plus a gauge term the loss never constrains. We propose GDSBM, which writes the control as a difference of vertex potentials and adds the action to the loss; pinning the gauge costs no expressiveness and makes the action a property of the model, so the penalty acts on the model and not on the gauge. On peptide generation our MadSBM reimplementation has a free-gauge action of order $10^{8}$ for a gauge-fixed value of $6.5$, against $1.5$ for GDSBM, with no quality loss that three seeds can detect. The gradient form also fits guidance, which becomes the addition of a potential: guided toward a net charge of $+3$ at pH~7, GDSBM is closer than MadSBM, over three seeds, to its exact tempered target in total variation at every guidance strength (at $\beta=1$, $81\%$ of samples in the target window against $74\%$, for a target of $97\%$); we claim no statistical significance.
item.dc:creator: Abdallah BenAbdallah, Mohsen Dlala

item.title: Control, stability, and stabilization of some classes of linear time-delay systems
item.description: arXiv:2610.31398v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This monograph presents a selection of the author's recent works on the control, stability, and stabilization of some classes of linear time-delay systems. After a detailed introduction to topics related to time-delay systems covered in the monograph, its main contents are presented in a series of mostly independent chapters.
item.dc:creator: Guilherme Mazanti

item.title: Benign cubic and quartic forms on the sphere
item.description: arXiv:2610.31403v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: One considers the NP-hard problem of minimizing real cubic and quartic forms on the Euclidean unit sphere. One first extends the Hessian spectral characterization of local minima by the author. In particular one provides a gap-depth characterization of negative global and spurious minima, and proves that the minimum value of an odd degree-d form is recovered (up to the factor d(d -1)) by minimizing the smallest eigenvalue of its ambient Hessian over the sphere (and equivalently the unit ball). Next, one exhibits several classes of benign families of cubic and quartic forms (i.e. with no spurious local minima on the sphere) and prove that some are robust to small coefficient perturbation (i.e. the resulting form remains benign even if it leaves the initial family). Therefore the class of benign cubic and quartic forms is full-dimensional (in the ambient space of coefficients), for n $\ge$ 2. Also for every odd degree d, the class of benign degree-d forms increases with the dimension (however it does not imply that such forms become more frequent when the dimension increases).
item.dc:creator: Jean B Lasserre (TSE-R, LAAS-POP)

item.title: A Resource Allocation Tournament
item.description: arXiv:2610.31418v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce and analyze a round-robin simultaneous resource allocation contest, motivated by sports leagues and other competitive environments where agents must distribute limited resources across multiple encounters. Players allocate resources in advance to matches against all opponents, and match outcomes are determined by relative allocations. We study two payoff schemes: total points, where players accumulate rewards for each win, and winner-takes-all, where only the tournament winner is rewarded. For three players, we provide complete equilibrium characterizations under both schemes. For four or more players, we show that the total points payoff admits Blotto-type equilibria, while the winner-takes-all payoff requires numerical and algorithmic analysis. To address this, we develop a best-response dynamics algorithm with stochastic inertia and use it to approximate equilibria in games with four and five players.
item.dc:creator: Adam Nathaniel, Refael Hassin

item.title: Effective Dual Subgradient Methods Through Sequential Subgradient-Aligned Rays
item.description: arXiv:2610.31486v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we propose an efficient subgradient-based framework, referred to as the sequential subgradient-aligned rays (SSAR) method, for improving the convergence performance of the dual subgradient method. In particular, the proposed method identifies and exploits a finite sequence of rays, when available, as the dual subgradient method evolves, along each of which a subgradient of the negative dual function remains constant and aligns with the ray. While the dual variable iterates remain on each identified ray, a constant stepsize associated with the ray is employed, with the associated constant stepsizes decreasing from one ray to the next. This approach yields constant decrements in the negative dual function values while the dual variable iterates remain on the associated rays, enabling the dual variable iterates to progress more quickly toward a dual optimal solution. We then show that the proposed SSAR method can be leveraged to improve the performance of the dual decomposition method for minimizing the average of local loss functions associated with multiple agents that share a common decision variable, a widely used problem formulation in many large-scale real-world applications. In particular, the SSAR method improves the convergence performance of the corresponding dual decomposition method while also reducing its communication cost. Numerical experiments on a least squares regression problem and a logistic regression problem using real datasets are conducted to evaluate the performance of the SSAR method.
item.dc:creator: Hansi Abeynanda, Chathuranga Weeraddana, Carlo Fischione

item.title: Douglas-Rachford splitting method for nonconvex stochastic optimal control
item.description: arXiv:2610.31502v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Motivated by the numerical resolution of stochastic optimal control problems, particularly those involving nonlinear dynamics, we investigate the convergence properties of the Douglas-Rachford splitting algorithm in a nonconvex and infinite-dimensional setting. We introduce an extension of the method that applies when one component of the objective function is continuously differentiable with a locally Lipschitz gradient, while the other is weakly lower semicontinuous with a bounded domain.
item.dc:creator: Fran\c{c}ois Caffier (IFPEN, DISCO), Paul Malisani (DISCO), Laurent Pfeiffer (DISCO)

item.title: Direct Inference on Admissible Sets (Diona)
item.description: arXiv:2610.31526v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose a new regression method named Direct Inference on Admissible Sets (Diona) that directly uses samples to estimate the state and its derivatives at a query point, along with their admissible bounds, without long global training. By casting the values and derivatives at the query and neighbouring samples as latent variables in a constrained optimisation problem, the burden of long training loops becomes one of on-demand local solves. We establish Diona's theoretical properties including finite-sample coverage and, in the noiseless case, convergence to the true state and derivatives under dense sampling. In a nonlinear regression benchmark on six functions of three to eight dimensions, Diona was more accurate than a Gaussian process (GP) on noiseless data especially with denser data sets. Furthermore, as with GP, it produced uncertainty bounds that contained the true value at more than 95% of query points in four functions. Diona's time to a first prediction after a data set update was three to four orders of magnitude shorter than that of the GP, and two to three orders shorter than that of a neural network, which was more accurate but offers no uncertainty quantification. This low latency is paid for by on-demand predictions, so this latency advantage applies when relatively few predictions are needed between data updates.
item.dc:creator: Lorenzo Sabug Jr., Eric Kerrigan

item.title: Learning SOCP Solver Dynamics with Graph Neural Networks
item.description: arXiv:2610.26285v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Second-order cone programs (SOCPs) are a fundamental class of convex optimization problems widely applied across engineering domains. Classical interior-point methods are robust and accurate, but their iterative nature can be costly in real-time or repeated-solve settings. This has motivated learning-based solvers that approximate optimizer solutions with neural networks. Recent work has increasingly studied graph neural networks (GNNs) for linear, quadratic, and second-order cone optimization, leveraging their ability to model sparse relational structure among variables, constraints, and objective functions. Most existing GNN-based solvers compress the optimization process into a single forward pass, predicting the optimizer directly without using the intermediate trajectory produced by classical solvers. We introduce SOCPNet, a recursive GNN framework that uses solver trajectories to learn an iterative SOCP solution procedure. A shared GNN model is applied repeatedly, refining the current iterate at each step and enabling inference for a variable number of iterations. Rather than predicting the solution in a single pass, SOCPNet learns from intermediate iterates to progressively refine its estimates using a trajectory-regularized training procedure. We evaluate SOCPNet on multiple datasets spanning standard SOCP problem classes and show that it consistently reduces the final solution error relative to a SOCP-GNN baseline. Finally, we demonstrate how trained SOCPNet models can be used in a hybrid optimization pipeline by warm-starting a classical interior-point solver, reducing solver iterations without loss of accuracy.
item.dc:creator: Adam Ghalem, Lou Sala\"un, Davide Rinaldi, Fragkiskos D. Malliaros

item.title: Dynamic Active Fleet Sizing of Heterogeneous UAV Relays for Post-Disaster Communication Networks
item.description: arXiv:2610.30323v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Uncrewed aerial vehicle (UAV) communication systems are increasingly used to provide temporary connectivity when ground communication infrastructure is damaged by disasters such as hurricanes and wildfires. However, the amount of aerial support required changes as ground networks recover and communication demand evolves. We focus on dynamically adjusting the number and allocation of actively deployed UAVs within a fixed available fleet. We develop a model predictive control (MPC) framework for dynamic fleet sizing of heterogeneous UAV relays during post-disaster communication recovery. The framework accounts for communication demand, ground network recovery, heterogeneous UAV operation, UAV energy availability, and backhaul capacity, which limits how much relayed traffic can be transmitted to the external communication network. The resulting formulation is a convex quadratic program that supports efficient online fleet sizing and deployment decisions. We evaluate the framework using seven historical disaster recovery case studies based on Federal Communications Commission reports, together with four backhaul scenarios and sensitivity analyses. Results show that required active UAV fleet size varies considerably throughout recovery, while backhaul capacity and fleet composition affect communication performance, highlighting the value of adapting active fleet size over time.
item.dc:creator: Jimin Choi, Max Z. Li

item.title: LLM2Cert: LLM Synthesis of Certificates with SMT/Lean Verification
item.description: arXiv:2610.30524v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Lyapunov functions and barrier certificates give state-space guarantees of stability and safety, but synthesizing and verifying them---especially for nonlinear, high-dimensional systems---remains an open challenge. Existing pipelines verify candidates with numerical solvers (sum-of-squares programs), interval methods, or satisfiability-modulo-theories (SMT) solvers, which often require relaxations, are conservative, or scale poorly with model dimension and nonlinearity. These limitations have also shaped benchmark design: standard test suites are dominated by low-dimensional polynomial systems chosen to suit what solvers can handle rather than what engineering applications require. We address both sides of this challenge. First, we introduce DynaCertBench, a benchmark of 105 instances: 80 non-redundant systems curated from the literature, extended with high-dimensional and control-constrained variants and new nonlinearly coupled systems, comprehensively spanning stability, region-of-attraction, forward-invariance, and safety tasks. Second, we present LLM2Cert, an LLM-driven framework that synthesizes candidate certificates and verifies them against their proof obligations: each obligation is routed to an SMT solver or directly to the Lean Proof-Repair agent. On DynaCertBench, LLM2Cert verifies 81 of 105 instances ($77.1\%$), a $17.1$ percentage point improvement over one-shot proposal without feedback. On the 81 fixed certificates, LLM2Cert verifies 22 that All-SMT leaves unresolved. Code and data are available at https://github.com/FormalCert-AI/llm2cert.
item.dc:creator: Zhipeng Cao, Peiyang Song, Nikolaus Vertovec, Weiru Cui, Zhihao Yang, Mingkang Liu, Luxia Lin, Bai Xue, Alessandro Abate

item.title: Deep ReLU Networks Can Fail the Best Approximation Property for Continuous Target Functions
item.description: arXiv:2610.31264v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We construct a continuous function on $[-1,1]^2$ for which the infimum of the $L^2$-approximation error over the class of ReLU networks with two hidden layers and architecture $(2,2,1,1)$ is not attained. This counterexample shows that deep ReLU networks do not satisfy the best approximation property in general, even for continuous target functions. Our findings contrast with existing results for shallow neural networks, where ReLU is one of the few activation functions that guarantee the existence of global minima in typical regression tasks. The proof is based on the fact that the breaklines for neurons in the second hidden layer can bend, which breaks the symmetry arguments used in the one-hidden-layer case.
item.dc:creator: Sebastian Kassing

item.title: Model Predictive Control of Wind Turbines: A Model-Oriented Review of Prediction Models, Control Objectives, and Nonlinear Aerodynamic Formulations
item.description: arXiv:2610.31295v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Model predictive control (MPC) has been applied to wind-turbine regulation with markedly different internal prediction models, ranging from linearized low-order turbine models to nonlinear, aeroelastic, floating, and data-driven predictors. This review organizes the literature primarily by the model propagated by the controller and treats model order, predictor representation, MPC formulation, control objective, and validation plant as separate descriptors. Primary studies show that low-order linear or piecewise-affine predictors are attractive for constrained power and speed regulation, whereas flexible drivetrain, structural, and floating models are needed when drivetrain twist, tower motion, blade loads, or platform dynamics are explicit control quantities. Nonlinear and economic MPC studies further demonstrate coordinated pitch/torque control across broad operating regions, while preview, repetitive, and data-driven formulations address wind prediction, periodic loads, and model mismatch. Particular attention is given to aerodynamic pitch dependence: variable-pitch turbine dynamics can be non-affine with respect to applied pitch, and the term NMPC alone does not prove that the original nonlinear pitch map is retained inside the optimizer. The review therefore adopts a conservative, equation-based classification for direct nonlinear applied-pitch propagation. Here, direct nonlinear applied-pitch propagation means that the applied pitch at each prediction step is evaluated inside the original nonlinear aerodynamic map, rather than replacing that dependence by a linearized, scheduled, piecewise-affine, or learned surrogate. The literature supports a remaining integration challenge at the intersection of flexible drivetrain prediction, nonlinear aerodynamic pitch treatment, explicit constraints and load objectives, and validated adaptive or learned model correction.
item.dc:creator: Roya Khalili-Amirabadi, Mohsen Jalaeian-Farimani, Mahdi Ghane

item.title: Dispersive Tree Agreements for Multi-Robot Coordination
item.description: arXiv:2610.31540v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Multi-robot coordination of nonlinear systems is naturally formulated as joint-space optimal control subject to constraints over groups of robots. Existing methods that approach joint optimality remain largely centralized, offline, and confined to collision-free motion planning, while decentralized, real-time counterparts target safe navigation without pursuing the joint optimum. This paper develops a decentralized, real-time planner that approaches the joint optimum as an anytime process. We extend a recent single-robot framework that searches dispersive trees of forward-propagated commands for differentially flat systems to coordinate a multi-robot team near-optimally. We first show that the inter-robot coupling can be effectively replaced by some local constraints, under which locally grown dispersive trees contain a near-optimal agreement. It is this structure that the robots pursue by decentralized column generation, negotiating rents on the shared space that guide the search of each robot's tree. The negotiation settles on an agreement whose near-optimality is certified at quiescence. Our protocol, WarpWeaver, implements this negotiation as an asynchronous real-time loop over a receding horizon, and demonstrates effective closure to quiesced agreements even when real-time deadlines cut the negotiation short. In simulation, WarpWeaver reduces total travel time by up to 22% against centralized offline planners on the Dynobench suite and by up to 37% against a decentralized real-time baseline, and nearly doubles the success rate of a task-specific planner on graph connectivity. Hardware experiments on six robots planning onboard demonstrate real-world implementability.
item.dc:creator: Shashank A. Deshpande, Blake T. Edwards, Jonathan P. How

item.title: ItsDEAL: Inexact two-level smoothing descent algorithms for weakly convex optimization
item.description: arXiv:2501.02155v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper addresses nonconvex optimization problems via a two-level smoothing framework, where the high-order Moreau envelope (HOME) provides a smooth approximation of weakly convex cost functions. We study the differentiability and weak smoothness of HOME. Building on the inexact two-level smoothing optimization framework (ItsOPT), we propose an inexact two-level smoothing descent algorithm (ItsDEAL) by: (i) approximately solving the proximal subproblem to obtain an inexact first-order oracle for HOME at the lower level; and (ii) applying an inexact first-order method at the upper level. We derive computable sufficient conditions for lower-level inexactness, enabling approximate high-order proximal-points to be certified without access to the exact proximal-point or HOME value. In particular, we study a parameter-free H\"olderian inexact gradient method and an inexact descent method with Armijo line search, both exploiting the weak smoothness of HOME. We establish subsequential convergence under mild inexactness assumptions, and global and linear convergence under the Kurdyka--{\L}ojasiewicz (KL) property. Preliminary experiments on ridge-regularized hinge-loss classification, a high-dimensional MCP-regularized classification model, and robust matrix completion illustrate the numerical behavior of the proposed methods and the role of the HOME order.
item.dc:creator: Alireza Kabgani, Masoud Ahookhosh

item.title: On the Gradient Domination of the LQG Problem
item.description: arXiv:2507.09026v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We consider solutions to the linear quadratic Gaussian (LQG) regulator problem via policy gradient (PG) methods. Although PG methods have demonstrated strong theoretical guarantees in solving the linear quadratic regulator (LQR) problem, despite its nonconvex landscape, their theoretical understanding in the LQG setting remains limited. Notably, the LQG problem lacks gradient dominance in the classical parameterization, i.e., with a dynamic controller, which hinders global convergence guarantees. In this work, we study a PG method for the LQG problem by adopting an alternative parameterization of the set of stabilizing controllers and employing a lifting argument. We refer to this parameterization as a history representation of the control input as it is parameterized by past input and output data from the previous p time-steps. Under this parameterization, the infinite-history LQG optimization reduces to an equivalent static state-feedback LQR problem, allowing us to recover gradient dominance and smoothness. For finite history length p, we establish model-based and model-free convergence guarantees up to a geometrically decaying history-truncation error.
item.dc:creator: Kasra Fallah, Leonardo F. Toso, James Anderson

item.title: Bayesian Ambiguity Contraction-based Adaptive Robust Markov Decision Processes for Adversarial Surveillance Missions
item.description: arXiv:2512.01660v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Collaborative Combat Aircraft (CCAs) are envisioned to enable autonomous Intelligence, Surveillance, and Reconnaissance (ISR) missions in contested environments, where adversaries may act strategically to deceive or evade detection. These missions pose challenges due to model uncertainty and the need for safe, real-time decision-making. Robust Markov Decision Processes (RMDPs) provide worst-case guarantees but are limited by static ambiguity sets that capture initial uncertainty without adapting to new observations. This paper presents an adaptive RMDP framework tailored to ISR missions with CCAs. We introduce a mission-specific formulation in which the CCA alternates between movement and sensing states. Adversarial uncertainty is represented by finite threat prototypes defining observation, exposure, and state-action transition models. Our approach incrementally refines policies by eliminating inconsistent threat models, allowing the CCA to move from worst-case protection toward more efficient mission policies while maintaining robustness. We establish fixed point stability, agreement with nominal planning as credible sets identify the true node-specific threat prototypes, and a conservative expected value guarantee while those prototypes remain credible. Experiments under Gaussian and non-Gaussian threat models across diverse network topologies show higher mission rewards and fewer exposure events compared to nominal and static robust planners.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: Journal of Guidance, Control, and Dynamics (2026)
item.dc:creator: Jimin Choi, Max Z. Li

item.title: OFF Newton-type Methods for Unconstrained Optimization with Inexact Derivatives
item.description: arXiv:2512.06825v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study objective-function-free (OFF) Newton-type methods for smooth unconstrained optimization with inexact gradients and Hessians. We propose two methods for first- and second-order stationarity, coupling explicit step-size rules with derivative-accuracy and linear-solver residual conditions to guarantee sufficient decrease without evaluating the objective function. The OFF regularized Newton method finds an $\varepsilon$-first-order stationary point in $\mathcal{O}(\varepsilon^{-2})$ iterations. Under strong convexity, a local Newton variant converges with \(Q\)-order at least $1+\theta$, where \(\theta \in (0, 1]\). For second-order stationarity, we combine regularized Newton steps with approximate eigenvectors associated with the minimum eigenvalue. With high probability, the resulting method finds an $(\varepsilon, \sqrt{L_h\varepsilon})$-second-order stationary point in $\mathcal{O}(\varepsilon^{-3/2})$ iterations, using a total of $\widetilde{\mathcal{O}}(\varepsilon^{-7/4})$ approximate gradient evaluations and Hessian-vector products. For finite-sum problems, we develop subsampling schemes that yield best-iterate convergence in expectation in the nonconvex first-order setting and local \(R\)-linear convergence with high probability in the strongly convex setting, followed by \(Q\)-order at least \(1+\theta\) once full sampling is reached. The subsampled second-order method achieves a high-probability $\widetilde{\mathcal{O}}(\varepsilon^{-7/2})$ total sample-operation bound, counting component gradient evaluations and component Hessian-vector products.
item.dc:creator: Hong Zhu

item.title: An efficient mixed-integer linear programming formulation for solving influence diagrams
item.description: arXiv:2601.08460v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Influence diagrams represent decision-making problems with interdependencies between random events, decisions, and consequences. Traditionally, they have been solved using tailored algorithms that determine the expected utility-maximizing decision strategy. Towards this end, most recent state-of-the-art solution approaches convert them into mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) models that can be solved using off-the-shelf MILP solvers. Computationally, these approaches are most efficient for influence diagrams that represent periodic (or sequential) decision processes, which can be cast as partially observable Markov Decision Processes. However, they are inefficient for problems that lack this periodic structure or whose influence diagrams have large state spaces. The efficient MILP formulation presented in this paper is specifically designed for influence diagrams that are challenging for earlier MILP formulations. Additionally, this formulation can be adapted to optimize conditional value-at-risk and to incorporate chance and logical constraints, thereby retaining the modeling flexibility of MILP-based methods. Finally, computational experiments on a range of problems from the literature are reported to show that the proposed formulation is much more efficient than earlier MILP formulations, particularly in problems which cannot be modeled as partially observable Markov decision processes and which lead to influence diagrams whose decision or chance nodes may have large state spaces.
item.dc:creator: Topias Terho, Fabricio Oliveira, Ahti Salo, Pedro Munari

item.title: Sinkhorn Distributionally Robust State Estimation via System Level Synthesis
item.description: arXiv:2602.08018v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In state estimation tasks, the usual assumption of an exactly known disturbance distribution is often unrealistic and renders the estimator fragile in practice. The recently emerging Wasserstein distributionally robust state estimation (DRSE) design can partially mitigate this fragility; however, its worst-case distribution is provably discrete, which deviates from the inherent continuity of real-world distributions and results in over-pessimism. In this work, we develop a new Sinkhorn DRSE design within the system level synthesis scheme with the aim of shaping the closed-loop errors under the unknown continuous disturbance distribution. For uncertainty description, we adopt the Sinkhorn ambiguity set that includes an entropic regularizer to penalize non-smooth and discrete distributions within a Wasserstein ball. We present the first result of finite-sample probabilistic guarantee of the Sinkhorn ambiguity set. Then we analyze the limiting properties of our Sinkhorn DRSE design, thereby highlighting its close connection with the generic $\mathcal{H}_2$ design and Wasserstein DRSE. To tackle the min-max optimization problem, we reformulate it as a finite-dimensional convex program through duality theory. By identifying a compact subset of the feasible set guaranteed to enclose the global optimum, we develop a tailored Frank-Wolfe solution algorithm and formally establish its convergence rate. The advantage of Sinkhorn DRSE over existing design schemes is verified through numerical case studies.
item.dc:creator: Yulin Feng, Xianyu Li, Steven X. Ding, Hao Ye, Chao Shang

item.title: Online Feedback Optimization for Constrained Stochastic Problems with Decision-Dependent Distributions
item.description: arXiv:2606.19284v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Online feedback optimization (OFO) leverages real-time output measurements to optimize the operation of networked systems without requiring full knowledge of system dynamics or disturbances. We develop an OFO approach for constrained stochastic optimization problems in which the distribution of the system's random parameters shifts in response to the control actions. We propose a projected primal-dual algorithm where the true dual constraint sets are replaced by surrogate sets. Our main result is an upper bound on the mean-square tracking error, which decomposes into four interpretable terms reflecting: (i) the stochasticity of the problem, (ii) output measurement errors, (iii) time-variability of the problem, and (iv) the mismatch between surrogate and true dual constraint sets. The theory is illustrated in a numerical experiment for power grids with price-responsive assets.
item.dc:creator: Caio Kalil Lauand, Emiliano Dall'Anese

item.title: Risk-Aware Unit Commitment in District Heating Networks: Chance-Constrained and CVaR Optimization Under Demand Uncertainty
item.description: arXiv:2608.10899v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: While district heating networks are a key component of the energy transition, their operational planning is challenging due to substantial uncertainty in heat demand. We study how unit-commitment schedules can account for this uncertainty and what reliability costs. By adapting chance-constrained programming (CC) and conditional value-at-risk (CVaR) optimization to the mixed-integer unit-commitment problem for district-heating networks, we can compute optimal unit-commitment schedules under demand uncertainty. We generate heat demand scenarios using a Bayesian model, which explicitly quantifies forecasting uncertainty and yields predictive distributions as input to the network optimization. To handle the inherent uncertainty in heat demand, we apply two stochastic optimization approaches that exploit this distribution: chance-constrained programming limits the probability of unmet demand, and in our scenario-based setting reduces to a deterministic MIP in which demand is replaced by an empirical quantile, while CVaR optimization penalizes severe shortfalls in the tail of the distribution. We evaluate the approaches both on real-world data from the Berlin district heating network and on a benchmark set of synthetic, realistically parameterized instances of varying sizes. The results show that the two methods are complementary: CC cheaply traces the high-reliability end of the cost--reliability trade-off and reveals the physical reliability limit of the network, whereas CVaR covers the low-cost, risk-tolerant regime at considerably higher computational effort.
item.dc:creator: Annika Buchholz, Janina Zittel, Thorsten Koch

item.title: When Is Two-Stage Sample Robust Optimization Asymptotically Optimal? A Simple Perspective
item.description: arXiv:2608.22999v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Two-stage sample robust optimization with linear decision rules is a standard data-driven approach to two-stage stochastic linear programs with unknown distributions. \cite{bertsimas2022two} established that this approach is asymptotically optimal under several conditions. Most conditions are mild, but one imposes a technical requirement on the recourse system. Whether this condition is implied by the others was left as an open question. We resolve this open question through a geometric feature of the support set: simpleness, the property that every vertex is incident to exactly as many edges as the dimension of the support. For simple support sets, the technical condition is automatic, and asymptotic optimality holds under the remaining standard assumptions. For every non-simple support, we construct a recourse system that is feasible everywhere in the support but violates the technical condition, and this construction resolves the open question. We further characterize the simpleness of one-sided and two-sided budgeted uncertainty sets and identify when budget perturbations can restore simpleness. We also develop a polynomial-time algorithm that certifies the technical condition at a given vertex using its incident edge directions. Numerical experiments on newsvendor and network lot-sizing problems illustrate the characterization and the effectiveness of the verification algorithm.
item.dc:creator: Ling Dai, Chin Pang Ho

item.title: Optimal Deterministic First-Order Oracle Complexity for Nonconvex-Concave Minimax Optimization
item.description: arXiv:2609.14235v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the deterministic first-order oracle complexity of smooth nonconvex-concave minimax optimization over a bounded convex dual domain under two notions of stationarity: optimization stationarity (OS) and game stationarity (GS). OS concerns stationarity of the value function, viewed as a structured nonsmooth objective obtained by maximizing over the dual variable. GS concerns the joint first-order optimality conditions for both primal minimization and dual maximization, each with the other variable held fixed. Existing upper bounds on the oracle complexity of first-order methods for finding $\epsilon$-OS and $\epsilon$-GS points have different dependence on $\epsilon$, but whether this difference reflects an intrinsic separation in computational hardness remains unresolved. We resolve this question by establishing worst-case lower bounds for arbitrary deterministic first-order methods: $\Omega(\epsilon^{-3})$ oracle queries for finding an $\epsilon$-OS point and $\Omega(\epsilon^{-5/2})$ for finding an $\epsilon$-GS point, with the remaining problem parameters fixed. These bounds match existing upper bounds up to logarithmic factors. To close the remaining logarithmic gap, we introduce Tracked-FOAM, a new first-order algorithm whose oracle complexity matches our lower bounds for both OS and GS. Together, these results establish an intrinsic separation between OS and GS in the optimal accuracy dependence of deterministic first-order oracle complexity.
item.dc:creator: Siyu Pan, Taoli Zheng, Jiajin Li

item.title: Optimal Network Dependence in Distributed Stochastic Optimization via Tree Routing
item.description: arXiv:2609.18101v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Communication is a central bottleneck in distributed optimization, but its effect is often summarized by the spectral gap of a chosen mixing matrix. Since this gap depends on link weights as well as topology, it can obscure the intrinsic effect of the network. We clarify this distinction by relating graph diameter to the inverse spectral gap. We establish a universal one-sided bound that is tight up to constant factors, while constructions across several graph families show that no topology-only converse or universal two-sided scaling law exists. This motivates a class-based view of network optimality: diameter-dependent guarantees can be assessed uniformly over graph classes, whereas spectral-gap optimality requires both the graph--matrix pair class and the admissible algorithm class to be specified.
